chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

He mentioned semen and treated it with greater strictness, and made it more severe than urine. Then he said: “If you see semen before, or after, entering into the salat (prayer), then you must repeat the salat (prayer). But if you looked at your garment and did not find it, then you prayed in it, and afterwards you saw it, then there is no repetition upon you; and likewise with urine.”

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ: repetition, meaning performing the salat (prayer) again
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act of worship whose repetition is discussed
key_terms.الْبَوْلِ: urine, mentioned here as sharing the same ruling in the latter case
key_terms.الْمَنِيَّ: semen, treated here as a substance whose presence on clothing affects the validity of salat (prayer)
key_terms.ثَوْبِكَ: your garment, the clothing being inspected for najasah
key_terms.رَأَيْتَ: you saw, indicating actual discovery of the impurity
key_terms.صَلَّيْتَ: you performed salat (prayer), referring to prayer done while unaware of the impurity

ai.seo_question: If I discover semen or urine on my clothing after salat (prayer), do I have to repeat the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding najasah found on one's garment in relation to salat (prayer). If semen is known to be present before or after entering the prayer, the prayer must be repeated, but if one had checked and not found it until after praying, then there is no repetition; the same ruling applies to urine in that case.
